extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, geometers, and analysts (users/teachers of fluxions and calculus)
extracted.subtask_description: A critical examination of the foundations and methods of fluxions (early calculus); queries and standards for what counts as clear, scientific, and admissible practice in geometry and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity_and_scientificness_of_method
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in order to arrive at these finite Lines proportional to the Fluxions, there be certain Steps made use of which are obscure and inconceivable, ... it must nevertheless be acknowledged, that your proceeding is not clear nor your method scientific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: representing fluxions by finite lines where intermediate steps are obscure or inconceivable renders the method unscientific and not clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_hidden_steps_when_substituting_finite_quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever is got by such Exponents and Proportions is to be ascribed to Fluxions: which must therefore be previously understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finite exponents or proportional finite lines are found by the help of fluxions, those fluxions must themselves be clearly defined and understood beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceivability_of_velocities_and_fluxions
rubrics_metrics.description: To form a precise Idea of a third Velocity for instance, in itself and by itself ... it is impossible. Measures and Signs are absolutely necessary, in order to conceive or reason about Velocities; and that, consequently, when we think to conceive the Velocities, simply and in themselves, we are deluded by vain Abstractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fluxions/velocities cannot be conceived apart from measures, time, space, and representative signs; demand caution with purely abstract formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_reifying_incomprehensible_entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Velocities of evanescent or nascent Quantities are supposed to be expressed ... but many who perhaps never having examined the matter, take it for granted, would upon a narrow scrutiny find it impossible to frame any Idea or Notion whatsoever of those Velocities exclusive of such finite Quantities and Signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat fluxions/infinitesimals as clear entities if their notion cannot be framed apart from symbols or finite measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagrams_as_signs_of_assignable_figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Diagrams in a Geometrical Demonstration are not to be considered, as Signs of all possible finite Figures, of all sensible and imaginable Extensions or Magnitudes of the same kind?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat diagrammatic lines as general signs representing all assignable finite figures of the same kind, rather than as absolute platonic entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_1:_Object_of_Geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Object of Geometry be not the Proportions of assignable Extensions? And whether, there be any need of considering Quantities either infinitely great or infinitely small?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Query framed to challenge use of infinites/unassignable magnitudes in geometry; encourages grounding geometry in proportions of assignable (finite) magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_2:_End_of_Geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the end of Geometry be not to measure assignable finite Extension? And whether this practical View did not first put Men on the study of Geometry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes practical objective of geometry as measurement of finite extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_3:_Mistaking_object_and_end
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the mistaking the Object and End of Geometry hath not created needless Difficulties, and wrong Pursuits in that Science?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that misconceiving the aim of geometry (e.g., focusing on infinitesimals) creates unnecessary complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_4:_Need_for_conceiving_object_end_method
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Men may properly be said to proceed in a scientific Method, without clearly conceiving the Object they are conversant about, the End proposed, and the Method by which it is pursued?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulates that scientific method requires clear conception of object, goal, and method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_5:_Assignable_numbers_and_divisibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it doth not suffice, that every assignable number of Parts may be contained in some assignable Magnitude? And whether it be not unnecessary, as well as absurd, to suppose that finite Extension is infinitely divisible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges the assumption of actual infinite divisibility of finite magnitudes; suggests sufficiency of assignable partitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_6:_Diagrams_as_representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Diagrams in a Geometrical Demonstration are not to be considered, as Signs of all possible finite Figures, of all sensible and imaginable Extensions or Magnitudes of the same kind?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates that diagrams should be treated as representative/general signs, not literal infinite objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_7:_Abstract_ideas_of_extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be possible to free Geometry from insuperable Difficulties and Absurdities, so long as either, the abstract general Idea of Extension, or absolute external Extension be supposed its true Object?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques reliance on an abstract absolute idea of extension as the cause of paradoxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_8:_Notions_of_absolute_time_place_motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Notions of absolute Time, absolute Place, and absolute Motion be not most abstractedly Metaphysical? Whether it be possible for us to measure, compute, or know them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether absolute constructs (time/place/motion) are measurable or suitable foundations for geometry/analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_9:_Engaging_in_unconceivable_disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Mathematicians do not engage themselves in Disputes and Paradoxes, concerning what they neither do nor can conceive? And whether the Doctrine of Forces be not a sufficient Proof of this?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against debates about notions that are not conceivably well-defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_10:_Sufficiency_of_assignable_finite_magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether in Geometry it may not suffice to consider assignable finite Magnitude, without concerning ourselves with Infinity? And whether it would not be righter to measure large Polygons having finite Sides, instead of Curves, than to suppose Curves are Polygons of infinitesimal Sides, a Supposition neither true nor conceivable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes preferring finite approximations (polygons) and avoiding conceiving curves as composed of infinitesimal parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_11:_Some_true_but_unpleasant_points
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether many Points, which are not readily assented to, are not nevertheless true? And whether those in the two following Queries may not be of that Number?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction to possibly counterintuitive but true positions; frames next queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_13:_Idea_of_extension_prior_to_motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be possible, that we should have had an Idea or Notion of Extension prior to Motion? Or whether if a Man had never perceived Motion, he would ever have known or conceived one thing to be distant from another?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether extension concept depends on perception of motion — challenges priors in geometric intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_13b:_Geometrical_quantity_coexistent_parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Geometrical Quantity hath coexistent Parts? And whether all Quantity be not in a flux as well as Time and Motion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions the static ontology of geometrical quantities; introduces flux-like conception of quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_14:_Extension_as_attribute_of_immutable_being
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Extension can be supposed an Attribute of a Being immutable and eternal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical challenge to metaphysical grounding of extension as attribute of an immutable being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_15:_Declining_examination_shows_bigotry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to decline examining the Principles, and unravelling the Methods used in Mathematics, would not shew a bigotry in Mathematicians?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates for critical examination of foundational principles rather than uncritical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_16:_Current_maxims_shocking_to_sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether certain Maxims do not pass current among Analysts, which are shocking to good Sense? And whether the common Assumption that a finite Quantity divided by nothing is infinite be not of this Number?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagging commonly accepted axioms/practices that may violate common sense (e.g., dividing by zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_17:_Considering_diagrams_absolutely
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the considering Geometrical Diagrams absolutely or in themselves, rather than as Representatives of assignable Magnitudes or Figures of the same, be not a principal Cause of the supposing finite Extension infinitely divisible; and of all the Difficulties and Absurdities consequent thereupon?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls to treat diagrams representatively to avoid conclusions about infinite divisibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_18:_Limiting_number_of_parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether from Geometrical Propositions being general, and the Lines in Diagrams being therefore general Substitutes or Representatives, it doth not follow that we may not limit or consider the number of Parts, into which such particular Lines are divisible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that generality of propositions does not force commitment to infinite divisibility; number of parts can be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_19:_Line_on_paper_contains_more_than_assignable_parts
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is said or implied, that such a certain Line delineated on Paper contains more than any assignable number of Parts, whether any more in truth ought to be understood, than that it is a Sign indifferently representing all finite Lines, be they ever so great? In which relative Capacity it contains, i.e. stands for more than any assignable number of Parts? And whether it be not altogether absurd to suppose a finite Line, considered in itself or in its own positive Nature, should contain an infinite number of Parts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges literal interpretation of diagrammatic lines as actually containing infinite parts; reiterates their role as signs representing all finite instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_20:_Arguments_for_infinite_divisibility_depend_on_abstract_ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether all Arguments for the infinite Divisibility of finite Extension do not suppose and imply, either general abstract Ideas or absolute external Extension to be the Object of Geometry? And, therefore, whether, along with those Suppositions, such Arguments also do not cease and vanish?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that arguments for infinite divisibility depend on metaphysical assumptions; removing those assumptions undermines the arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_21:_Infinite_divisibility_as_snare
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the supposed infinite Divisibility of finite Extension hath not been a Snare to Mathematicians, and a Thorn in their Sides? And whether a Quantity infinitely diminished and a Quantity infinitely small are not the same thing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that the notion of infinite divisibility causes confusion; equates certain infinitary concepts as problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_22:_Necessity_of_velocities_nascent_increments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be necessary to consider Velocities of nascent or evanescent Quantities, or Moments, or Infinitesimals? And whether the introducing of Things so inconceivable be not a reproach to Mathematics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether nascent/evanescent/infinitesimal entities are necessary or appropriate in mathematical foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_23:_Can_inconsistencies_be_truths
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Inconsistencies can be Truths? Whether Points repugnant and absurd are to be admitted upon any Subject, or in any Science? And whether the use of Infinites ought to be allowed, as a sufficient Pretext and Apology, for the admitting of such Points in Geometry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether admitting paradoxical or inconsistent entities (e.g., infinitesimals) is acceptable in a scientific discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_24:_Knowing_quantity_via_proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a Quantity be not properly said to be known, when we know its Proportion to given Quantities? And whether this Proportion can be known, but by Expressions or Exponents, either Geometrical, Algebraical, or Arithmetical? And whether Expressions in Lines or Species can be useful but so far forth as they are reducible to Numbers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes proportions and reducibility to numerical expressions as the basis of knowing quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_25:_Proper_expressions_and_arithmetical_operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the finding out proper Expressions or Notations of Quantity be not the most general Character and Tendency of the Mathematics? And Arithmetical Operation that which limits and defines their Use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights the centrality of finding good notations/expressions and the role of arithmetic operations in defining their applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_26:_Analogy_and_use_of_signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Mathematicians have sufficiently considered the Analogy and Use of Signs? And how far the specific limited Nature of things corresponds thereto?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for critical attention to how signs/notations map to the limited nature of concrete things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_27:_Algebraic_licence_in_geometrical_cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether because, in stating a general Case of pure Algebra, we are at full liberty to make a Character denote, either a positive or a negative Quantity, or nothing at all, we may therefore in a geometrical Case, limited by Hypotheses and Reasonings from particular Properties and Relations of Figures, claim the same Licence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether algebraic freedoms of symbol interpretation legitimately transfer to geometrical reasoning constrained by specific hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_28:_Shifting_of_hypothesis_as_sophism
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Shifting of the Hypothesis, or (as we may call it) the fallacia Suppositionis be not a Sophism, that far and wide infects the modern Reasonings, both in the mechanical Philosophy and in the abstruse and fine Geometry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies a common fallacy — altering hypotheses mid-reasoning — as pervasive and dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_29:_Can_velocity_be_conceived_without_measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether we can form an Idea or Notion of Velocity distinct from and exclusive of its Measures, as we can of Heat distinct from and exclusive of the Degrees on the Thermometer, by which it is measured? And whether this be not supposed in the Reasonings of modern Analysts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges analysts who treat velocity as an entity independent of its measurable indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_30:_Motion_and_velocity_in_a_point_of_space
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Motion can be conceived in a Point of Space? And if Motion cannot, whether Velocity can? And if not, whether a first or last Velocity can be conceived in a mere Limit, either initial or final, of the described Space?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions meaningfulness of assigning motion/velocity to idealized points or limit positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_31:_Ratios_without_increments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are no Increments, whether there can be any Ratio of Increments? Whether Nothings can be considered as proportional to real Quantities? Or whether to talk of their Proportions be not to talk Nonsense? Also in what Sense we are to understand the Proportion of a Surface to a Line, of an Area to an Ordinate? And whether Species or Numbers, though properly expressing Quantities which are not homogeneous, may yet be said to express their Proportion to each other?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges the coherence of ratios involving non-existent (zero/infinitesimal) increments and cross-dimensional proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_32:_Squaring_circles_and_parabolas_via_assignable_cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether if all assignable Circles may be squared, the Circle is not, to all intents and purposes, squared as well as the Parabola? Or whether a parabolical Area can in fact be measured more accurately than a Circular?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probe into comparative measurability of various curves and implications of squaring assignable instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_33:_Approximation_vs_sophism_for_accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it would not be righter to approximate fairly, than to endeavour at Accuracy by Sophisms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates honest approximation over achieving 'accuracy' via fallacious reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_34:_Trials_and_inductions_vs_false_principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it would not be more decent to proceed by Trials and Inductions, than to pretend to demonstrate by false Principles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports empirical/inductive methods over demonstrations resting on dubious principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_35:_Knack_vs_science_when_principles_not_scientific
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there be not a way of arriving at Truth, although the Principles are not scientific, nor the Reasoning just? And whether such a way ought to be called a Knack or a Science?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether success despite faulty principles should be labelled technique (knack) rather than genuine science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_36:_Science_of_conclusion_vs_principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there can be Science of the Conclusion, where there is not Science of the Principles? And whether a Man can have Science of the Principles, without understanding them? And therefore whether the Mathematicians of the present Age add like Men of Science, in taking so much more pains to apply their Principles, than to understand them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insists that understanding principles is prerequisite for scientific conclusions; critiques overemphasis on application over comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_37:_Genius_vs_false_principles_and_quadratures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the greatest Genius wrestling with false Principles may not be foiled? And whether accurate Quadratures can be obtained without new Postulata or Assumptions? And if not, whether those which are intelligible and consistent ought not to be preferred to the contrary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that genius cannot compensate for false premises; recommends adopting intelligible and consistent assumptions for quadrature problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_38:_Tedious_calculations_and_improvement_of_mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether tedious Calculations in Algebra and Fluxions be the likeliest Method to improve the Mind? And whether Mens being accustomed to reason altogether about Mathematical Signs and Figures, doth not make them at a loss how to reason without them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions educational value of mechanical symbol-manipulation and whether it degrades broader reasoning skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query_39:_Transferability_of_analysts_skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, whatever readiness Analysts acquire in stating a Problem, or finding apt Expressions for Mathematical Quantities, the same doth necessarily infer a proportionable ability in conceiving and expressing other Matters?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether facility in symbolic or formal manipulation implies comparable ability in other domains of thought.
